title: Unbounded Cardinality in Metrics Labels
pattern: Inserting highly dynamic, unbounded fields (such as user IDs, session tokens, request UUIDs, or raw URL strings) as labels or dimensions in TSDB metrics counters.
why_bad: In-memory metric collectors represent each unique label combination as a distinct time-series object [351]. Using dynamic, high-cardinality values as labels causes the number of active metrics series to grow exponentially [351]. This silently consumes all application RAM, degrading garbage-collection performance and causing OOM crashes [351, 535].
detection: Identify counter or histogram registration functions that bind runtime dynamic string parameters (e.g., parameters that contain random UUIDs, email addresses, or user keys) as labels.
fix: Only use bounded, low-cardinality categories as metric labels. Store high-cardinality fields in logs or trace contexts instead [351, 535].
source: Brendan Gregg, *Systems Performance*, Chapter 4 / passage [351]; Martin Kleppmann, *Designing Data-Intensive Applications*, Chapter 11 / passage [535].
